newsitem.title: USA: Doubletree to buy Renaissance for $850 million.
newsitem.headline: Doubletree to buy Renaissance for $850 million.

text.p: Hotel operator Doubletree Corp. said Tuesday it planned to buy Renaissance Hotel Group NV in an $850 million stock-and-cash deal that should boost its domestic presence and take it abroad.
Phoenix-based Doubletree, which completed its $1.2 billion purchase of Red Lion Hotels Inc. in November, will expand around the globe with its purchase of Hong Kong-based Renaissance.
"It happened a lot faster than I expected, particularly after they just finished closing the Red Lion deal," said John Rohs, an analyst with Schroder Wertheim & Co.
"But this deal fits nicely with Doubletree's strategy toward an upscale orientation in the U.S. and meaningful exposure overseas. It will complement an already strong domestic position," said Rohs.

Doubletree, the exclusive franchisor of Doubletree Hotels, Doubletree Guest Suites and Club Hotels by Doubletree, currently, owns, leases manages or franchises about 235 hotels in the United States, Mexico and the Caribbean.
Earlier in 1996 Doubletree acquired RFS Inc., a privately held hotel operator.

Renaissance operates about 140 hotels, including 75 Renaissance luxury hotels, 12 New World upscale hotels and 51 Ramada mid-priced hotels, in North and South America, Europe and the Asia-Pacific region.
The latest deal calls for Doubletree to buy all of Renaissance's outstanding and issued shares for a combination of $8 in cash and 0.4105 Doubletree share for each Renaissance share.
Analysts said the latest deal, if completed, would rank Doubletree in the same league with Hilton Hotels Corp., which is the seventh largest U.S. hotel management company.
The top two leading U.S. hotel management companies are New Jersey-based HFS Inc. and Bass Plc's Holiday Inn, respectively, according to analysts.
Doubletree's escalating acquisition pace comes at an appropriate time, they said.
"The hotel industry has been a healthy industry for a couple of years due to a slowdown in construction of new hotel properties," said Bruce Thorp of PNC Institutional Investment Services.
He said demand and occupancy rates have been rising as supply growth has slowed. "We see this continuing through 1997, although property construction is beginning to creep up," he said.
Nevertheless, analysts said they expected further acquisitions from Doubletree.
Renaissance shares were up $7.125 at $23.50 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange. Doubletree shares traded down $3.875 at $43.625 on Nasdaq.

The $850 million purchase price was based on a ratio of 0.4105 Doubletree shares, with each Doubletree share valued at $42.15, a price that both companies agreed to. The total also included $70 million in debt, they said.

The New World Group, which owns about 54.4 percent of Renaissance's outstanding shares, has indicated its intention to tender its shares to the proposed offer and to vote its shares in favor of the proposed transaction, the companies said.
